description: Split 'make it stop' into a deterministic cancel of a not-yet-executing AgentTurn and a Runtime stop request of an executing AgentTurn, addressed at a specific Turn with an honest Unknown state and one shared Web/CLI vocabulary.

tasks.title: Durable follow-up Turn records and turn-keyed transitions
tasks.spec: specs/agent-turn-cancel/spec.md#Cancel is deterministic and does not contact the Runtime
tasks.description: Generalize the Session Turn model from the initial-launch-only MarkInitialTurn* surface to Turn-id-keyed transitions any Turn can use, and record a durable Queued AgentTurn (stable id, linked to its accepted SessionInput) when a follow-up starts an idle turn, before Runner dispatch. Existing launch and terminal flows delegate to the new surface unchanged. Add a Server-only CancelTurn transition and a shared turn-control resolver (find-by-id + terminal/queued/executing classification) that later cancel/stop operations build on.
acceptanceCriteria: A follow-up that starts an idle turn persists exactly one AgentTurnRecord with a stable id in Queued status, linked to its accepted SessionInput, before any Runner dispatch; the Runner does not create a duplicate session.input record for that turn.
A repeated or redispatched follow-up for the same accepted input does not create a second Turn; the recorded Turn id survives Server restart.

MarkTurnExecuting and MarkTurnTerminal are keyed by Turn id; the AgentJob launch path delegates via its stored InitialTurnId and behaves identically to today (Queued to Executing, terminal mapping, activity convergence, no-op on an already-terminal Turn).
CancelTurn(turnId) flips Queued to Cancelled on the Server with no Runner or Runtime contact and converges Session activity to idle; it is a no-op on an already-terminal or Executing Turn.
The shared turn-control resolver returns the target Turn's current status and a terminal/queued/executing classification, returning turn-not-found for an unknown id, without mutating state.
Existing launch, follow-up join-active-turn, recovery (compact/reset), and terminal-close flows continue to pass unchanged.

Server spec tests cover idle-start Turn recording, no-duplicate on retry, turn-keyed executing/terminal transitions, CancelTurn determinism and no-op guards, restart identity preservation, and unchanged launch/follow-up/recovery behaviour, using fake time, storage, and dispatch observers; npm test passes.
tasks.output: Follow-up idle-start Turn recording; turn-id-keyed Session transition surface with CancelTurn; shared turn-control resolver; AgentJob launch delegation.
tasks.notes: Implements design D1-D2 and is the prerequisite for both cancel and stop. It records only the current Turn (bounded by the at-most-one-active-Turn invariant); it does not retroactively record historical Turns and adds no cancel/stop endpoint.

tasks.title: Deterministic cancel of a queued Turn (Server)
tasks.spec: specs/agent-turn-cancel/spec.md#First-Turn cancel adjudicates the owning AgentJob as cancelled
tasks.description: Add AgentJobStatus.Cancelled (terminal) and AgentJob.CancelAsync, and wire the Session cancel path. The cancel grain operation resolves the target Turn via the T-001 resolver: a terminal Turn returns turn-already-ended; a Queued launch Turn delegates to its AgentJob (Pending to Cancelled, no dispatch, then marks the Turn Cancelled); a Queued later Turn is cancelled directly on the Session; an Executing Turn is rejected for cancel. Expose POST /agent-sessions/{id}/cancel with a turnId body. Cancel never contacts the Runner.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /agent-sessions/{sessionId}/cancel with a turnId cancels a Queued Turn deterministically on the Server and returns state cancelled; it succeeds even when no Runner is bound and issues no Runner or Runtime request.

Cancelling the launch Turn while its AgentJob is Pending transitions the Job to AgentJobStatus.Cancelled (terminal, no dispatch) and records the first Turn as Cancelled rather than Failed; IsTerminal includes Cancelled and Unknown remains non-terminal.

The cancel/dispatch race is decided inside the AgentJob grain: if the Job already dispatched (Turn Executing) the cancel is rejected and the caller is directed to stop; if cancel wins the Job never dispatches.
Cancelling a later (follow-up) Turn does not contact or rewrite an already-terminal AgentJob; the Turn goes Cancelled and the Job verdict is unchanged.
A cancel against an already-terminal Turn returns turn-already-ended with the Turn's terminal status, issues no Runner request, and touches no other Turn.
A cancel against an Executing Turn is not applied as a cancel and reports the honest current state.

The cancelled Turn record, its SessionInput records, the AgentSession, transcript, and lineage remain present and readable; after cancelling the only non-terminal Turn the Session activity is idle and a subsequently accepted input starts a new Turn.
All enum projections (list, capacity, observation) handle AgentJobStatus.Cancelled, and architecture tests assert only the Job resolves first-Turn terminal from its own facts.

Server tests cover queued cancel, first-Turn Job cancellation, the cancel/dispatch race in both outcomes, later-Turn cancel leaving a terminal Job, stale entry, Executing-Turn rejection, and record preservation, with fakes only; npm test passes.
tasks.output: AgentJobStatus.Cancelled and AgentJob.CancelAsync; Session cancel grain operation; POST /agent-sessions/{id}/cancel with turnId and stale-guard; first-Turn cancelled terminal mapping.
tasks.notes: Implements design D3 plus the cancel half of D5. The Session grain delegates launch-Turn cancel to the Job so dispatch and cancel serialize in one grain; later-Turn cancel is Session-only. Cancel is Server-only; no cancel SignalR method is introduced.

tasks.title: Runtime stop request of an executing Turn (Server + Runner)
tasks.spec: specs/agent-turn-stop/spec.md#Stop requests the Runtime to halt a specific executing Turn
tasks.description: Repurpose the existing cancel transport as the stop path. POST /agent-sessions/{id}/stop carries a turnId; the grain resolves the Turn via the T-001 resolver and applies stop only to an Executing Turn (a Queued Turn is rejected with use-cancel; a terminal Turn returns turn-already-ended). The runner keeps its binding-guarded abort and idle/unknown activity convergence, but its reply and the HTTP response adopt the new vocabulary: confirmed stop to stopped, unconfirmed to unknown with interruptUnconfirmed, request-sent-not-yet-confirmed to stop-requested. First-Turn stop continues to be adjudicated by the AgentJob through the normal result-report/Unknown path; later-Turn stop never touches the Job.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /agent-sessions/{sessionId}/stop with a turnId sends a stop request to the bound Runtime for an Executing Turn and mirrors the state the Runtime actually observed; it is presented as a request, not an immediately guaranteed halt.
A stop against a Queued Turn issues no Runtime request and directs the caller to cancel; a stop against an already-terminal Turn returns turn-already-ended and touches no other Turn.

The runner reply and HTTP response use stopped for a confirmed stop (not cancelled), unknown with interruptUnconfirmed for an unconfirmed stop, and stop-requested when the request was sent but halt not yet confirmed; the API never fakes a successful stop.

An unconfirmed stop leaves the target Turn and the AgentSession activity Unknown; no new Turn is created, no accepted SessionInput is replayed, and no idle/completed/failed verdict is synthesised; Unknown reconciles only on authoritative Runtime evidence.
A later-Turn stop does not rewrite an already-terminal AgentJob; Turn result and AgentJob status remain independent facts.
The stopped Turn record, its SessionInput records, the transcript, and any partial output captured before the stop remain present and readable.
The runner stop handler retains its binding-guarded session.activity outbox fact (confirmed to idle, unconfirmed to unknown) and remains available while the durable snapshot is being recovered.

Server and Runner tests cover Executing-Turn stop (confirmed and unconfirmed), Queued-Turn rejection, stale entry, Unknown preservation with no replay, later-Turn Job isolation, and record preservation, using a fake Runtime and fake Server connection; npm test, npm run typecheck -w packages/runner, and npm test -w packages/runner pass.
tasks.output: POST /agent-sessions/{id}/stop with turnId and stale-guard; Session stop grain operation; runner stop reply and HTTP response remapped to stopped/unknown/stop-requested; existing honesty machinery retained.
tasks.notes: Implements design D4 plus the stop half of D5. It reuses the existing CancelAgentSession transport, abort, and binding-guarded activity convergence; the change is turn targeting, the stale-guard, and the vocabulary remap. It does not depend on the cancel task (T-002).

tasks.title: Web and CLI cancel/stop experience with one vocabulary
tasks.spec: specs/agent-turn-control-surface/spec.md#Web and CLI share one cancel and stop vocabulary
tasks.description: Surface cancel and stop in CLI and Web with one shared vocabulary. CLI exposes mo session cancel (deterministic cancel of a queued Turn) and mo session stop (Runtime stop request of an executing Turn) as distinct operations; the prior mo session cancel stop semantics are removed. Web adds a Turn-level cancel/stop control in the coder-session widget. Both clients render cancelled/stop-requested/stopped/unknown from the Server reply with identical meaning and offer the same verification entry for unknown.
acceptanceCriteria: mo session cancel posts to the cancel endpoint with a turnId and applies only to a queued Turn; mo session stop posts to the stop endpoint with a turnId and requests a Runtime stop of an executing Turn; help text distinguishes a deterministic cancel from a runtime stop request.
CLI renders cancelled, stop-requested, stopped, and unknown from the Server reply and, for unknown, points to the same verification entry as Web.
Web exposes a Turn-level cancel/stop control that targets the current Turn and renders the same four labels with the same meaning.
Web and CLI use the same label for each outcome and never infer a Turn or AgentJob result from Session activity.
The previous mo session cancel stop semantics are removed (BREAKING) and no second control surface is introduced.
Web tests cover cancel/stop control targeting, the four labels, and the unknown verification entry; CLI tests cover both verbs, turnId forwarding, and the shared output shape.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web, npm run test:run -w packages/web, npm run check:fsd -w packages/web, and npm test pass.
tasks.output: mo session cancel and mo session stop verbs with shared output; Web Turn-level cancel/stop control and shared label rendering; aligned unknown verification entry.
tasks.notes: Implements the client portion of design D6. Server-side reply labels are owned by T-002 (cancel) and T-003 (stop); this task renders them consistently and adds no new server authority.
